## Getting there

**Route Planner**

We encourage you to go green when planning your visit: the Belvedere is easily reached by public transportation, and offers as well a charging station for electric cars, a city bike station, and bicycle racks in the immediate vicinity.

**Contact**

### Information Desk

T: [+43 1 795 57-0](tel:+43179557-0)

E-Mail: [**info@belvedere.at**](mailto:info@belvedere.at)

**Address**

Prinz-Eugen-Straße 27, 1030 Vienna

**Public Transport**

**Tram D** 
Station „Schloss Belvedere“ 
**Train & S-Bahn, Tram 18, O** 
Station „Quartier Belvedere“ 
**Underground U1** 
Station „Südtiroler Platz / Hauptbahnhof“ & walkway around 15 minutes

**Bike**

Bike parking in the palace gardens, Entrances Prinz-Eugen-Straße and Landstraßer Gürtel,

**Car**

Discounted parking for a time of 6 hours is offered by the BIP Garage at Palais Schwarzenberg and the BIP Garage Schwarzenbergplatz. Note: This discount does not apply with the parking app.

[Location map Upper Belvedere](https://www.belvedere.at/sites/default/files/2026-06/location-map-ob.jpg)

[Google Streetview](https://artsandculture.google.com/search/streetview?p=belvedere)

[Floorplan Upper Belvedere](https://www.belvedere.at/sites/default/files/2026-10/Map_OB_0.jpg)

## Gardens

### Gardens

The Belvedere’s garden is one of Europe’s most significant historical gardens and is a fine example of late Baroque garden design.

[More](https://www.belvedere.at/en/belvedere/gardens)

# Visit

Get all the information you need for your visit.

## Venues of the Belvedere

[More about Upper Belvedere](https://www.belvedere.at/en/visit/upper-belvedere)

### Upper Belvedere

Baroque palace and 800 years of art history - with masterpieces by Klimt, Schiele, Funke, Messerschmidt and van Gogh.

[Plan your visit](https://www.belvedere.at/en/visit/upper-belvedere) [Tickets](https://www.belvedere.at/en/go/tickets)

[More about Lower Belvedere](https://www.belvedere.at/en/visit/lower-belvedere)

### Lower Belvedere

Art exhibitions from all periods at the former residential palace of Prince Eugene and at the Orangery. Treasures from the Middle Ages await you in the Palace Stables.

[Plan your visit](https://www.belvedere.at/en/visit/lower-belvedere) [Tickets](https://www.belvedere.at/en/go/tickets)

[More about Belvedere 21](https://www.belvedere.at/en/visit/belvedere-21)

### Belvedere 21

The venue for contemporary Austrian and international art, film, and music. Architectural icon of post-war Modernism.

[Plan your visit](https://www.belvedere.at/en/visit/belvedere-21) [Tickets](https://www.belvedere.at/en/go/tickets)

### Bundesmuseen Card € 99

The Bundesmuseen Card provides access to all participating museums for one year. The Bundesmuseen Card is an initiative of the Federal Ministry of Houseing, Art, Culture, Media and Sport.

[Buy](https://www.belvedere.at/tickets?location[]=annual) [More](https://www.belvedere.at/en/node/12102)

## Further Informations

**Time slot and day tickets for the Belvedere**

The visit to the Upper and Lower Belvedere is only possible with a valid time slot ticket. For the Belvedere 21 you need to choose the day of your visit. Combination tickets are available as day tickets with a time slot for our most visited location the Upper Belvedere. You may visit the other locations on the same day before or after the booked time slot. Select your time slot according to availability when you buy your ticket online or at the ticket office. The duration of your visit is not limited.

You don't need a time slot or day ticket and can go directly to the entrance if you present one of the following tickets or membership cards and a valid ID:

- Belvedere [Gold Pass](https://www.belvedere.at/en/goldpass)

- [Friends](https://www.belvedere.at/en/support/friends-belvedere) of the Belvedere card

- [Bundesmuseen Card](https://www.belvedere.at/en/node/12102)

- Vienna Pass or Flexi Pass

- ICOM Membership Card

We are looking forward to your visit!

[Tickets](https://www.belvedere.at/en/tickets)

**Kulturpass**

The _Kulturpass_ entitles you to free museum admission and a complimentary audio guide.

People at risk of poverty in Austria, asylum seekers and refugees holding a displaced person's ID are entitled to a so-called _Kulturpass_ from the _Aktion Hunger auf Kunst und Kultur_. Click [here](https://www.hungeraufkunstundkultur.at/jart/prj3/hakuk/main.jart?reserve-mode=reserve&content-id=1482242680324&rel=de) to download the _Kulturpass_ mobile app.

You can pick up your free ticket at one of our offices.

**Bundesmuseen Card**

The new Bundesmuseen Card provides access to all participating museums for one year. The Bundesmuseen Card is an initiative of the Federal Ministry of Houseing, Art, Culture, Media and Sport.

[More](https://www.bundesmuseencard.at/)

**IAA Card**

Free admission to our museums with a the [IAA Card](https://www.iaa-europe.eu/index.php/iaa-card).

Obtain your free ticket at one of our offices by presenting your membership card.

**Audio Guides**

In the Upper Belvedere Audio guides are available by the ticket counter in: Cantonese, English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Mandarin, Polish, Russian, Spanish, Ukrainian

In the Lower Belvedere Audio guides for specific exhibitions are available by the ticket counter in: German and English

We ask that you use personal headphones (standard 3.5 mm connection). Disposable headphones can be purchased if available.

**Rental Fees** 
Permanent collection tour Upper Belvedere: € 5,00 
Exhibition tour Lower Belvedere: € 5,00

**FAQ**

Is there anything we can help you with? Here are some answers to frequently asked questions.

[More](https://www.belvedere.at/en/faq)

**Go Green**

We encourage you to go green when planning your visit: the Belvedere is easily reached by public transportation, and offers as well a charging station for electric cars, a city bike station, and bicycle racks in the immediate vicinity.

[More](https://www.belvedere.at/en/belvedere/green-belvedere)

**Accessibility for all Visitors**

The museum aims to be easily accessible to everyone. Visitors with disabilities are supported in experiencing our programs through sensory-friendly resources. All restroom facilities are gender-neutral to prevent discrimination.

[More](https://www.belvedere.at/en/your-visit/inclusion-museum)

**Book your private guided tour online**

Planning a group visit to the museum? Choose from our range of tours and contact us to schedule an appointment.

[Program](https://www.belvedere.at/en/on-request-groups)

[More about FAQ](https://www.belvedere.at/en/faq)

### Un musée conçu par Victor Horta

Le Musée des Beaux-Arts abrite la formidable collection d’Henri Van Cutsem, comprenant notamment les deux seules œuvres d’Édouard Manet conservées en Belgique.

## Actualités

Passer le slider

- 06 octobre 2026

 ### Exposition Manet. Jamais vu, Manet

 Une nouvelle grande exposition prévue pour la fin de l'année.

- 30 avril 2026

 ### Nuit des musées 2026

 La nuit des musées est de retour ce 16 mai 2026 pour vous faire découvrir les musées de la ville en soirée.

- 16 décembre 2025

 ### Nouvelle exposition : "Cortèges"

 Une centaine de sculptures prennent vie dans l'Atrium du Musée

- 03 juin 2025

 ### La Fanfunambule s'installe au musée ce 15 juin !

 Ce dimanche 15 juin à 18h00 ou à 19h30, assistez à une concert de la fanfare détournée et des passeurs de rêves.

- 19 mai 2025

 ### Dimanche + que gratuit au musée ce 1er juin!

- 15 mai 2025

 ### Le groupe U-Dada sera présent au musée ce 17 mai !

 Le quatuor franco-belge U-Dada, composé de Maxime Bivort, David Bouquelle, Benjamin Paris et Martin Vancoppenolle, sera présent au musée durant la nuit des musées ce 17 mai.

- 05 mai 2025

 ### Nuit des musées 2025 au Musée des Beaux-Arts

 La nuit des musées est de retour en 2025 pour vous faire découvrir les musées de la ville en soirée.

- 03 mars 2025

 ### La programmation 2025 est en ligne !

 Découvrez nos rendez-vous de 2025...

- 14 janvier 2025

 ### Collaboration entre le RAMDAM Festival et le Musée des Beaux-Arts !

 Projection et visites exclusives ce 19 et 25 janvier en collaboration avec le RAMDAM Festival !

[Voir tout](https://mba.tournai.be/actualites-mba 'Actualités du musée des Beaux-Arts')

# The Art Alliance museums

A masterpiece that leaves you speechless. A building that makes an impression even before you step inside. Art in the middle of the woods, by the sea or in the heart of a historical town. In the Netherlands, art and culture are everywhere and close at hand. With the 16 outstanding and surprising museums across the Netherlands listed below, the Art Alliance showcases what our country has to offer. Because wherever you are in the Netherlands, there’s always a museum to suit your interests and your travel style.

- Discover art, design, and stories throughout the Netherlands.
- Enrich your holiday with a visit to a museum.
- Get going with these surprising tips from the Art Alliance.

## Dutch Masters or modern

© Koen Smilde via Iamsterdam

Come face to face with Rembrandt, Vermeer, Frans Hals and Van Gogh. Artists who forever changed the way we see the Netherlands. Their work is famous the world over. Seeing the Dutch Masters in real life is truly awe-inspiring. Admire masterpieces at the Rijksmuseum in Amsterdam or the Mauritshuis in The Hague. In Haarlem, discover just how lively Frans Hals’s portraits still are. Ideal for a city break packed with history, beautiful streets and canals, and unforgettable art. And in the middle of our country, you can immerse yourself in Rietveld’s remarkable works.

On the other hand, it is modern art that really challenges us and offers a glimpse into the world of tomorrow. In creative cities such as Rotterdam and Arnhem, you’ll find museums that focus on new ideas and perspectives. The Kunsthal in Rotterdam is constantly changing its perspective and subject matter. And in that very same city, you’ll be surprised by the extraordinary Depot Boijmans van Beuningen. The building itself is an architectural work of art, both inside and out. And in Arnhem, you could visit Museum Arnhem and combine it with a meal at a good restaurant or a relaxing afternoon in the city. You don’t have to understand everything straight away. That's precisely what makes it powerful.

© Iris van den Broek

## Heritage and stories

© Eva Broekema via Kröller-Müller Museum

A city or region becomes more interesting once you know its stories: old façades are no longer merely beautiful, squares take on meaning and landscapes begin to speak. You see things in a different light and discern details you wouldn’t have noticed before. If you’re cycling through the Veluwe, be sure to visit the Kröller-Müller Museum and wander through the extensive sculpture garden. Amidst works of art, forests and open fields, you’ll experience how culture and nature complement each other and present new perspectives.

In Leeuwarden, ceramics, regional stories and international influences come together. The Stedelijk Museum Breda has a contemporary view of the city and its society, whilst in Limburg you can discover more about the culture, traditions and history of this distinctive region. This adds an extra dimension to every destination, allowing you to take home more than just lovely memories. A visit to a museum simply helps you to understand places better.

© Mijke Bos via Merkfryslan Royal

Category: Visit website

Category: Visit website

## Surprising collections

© Marjon Gemmeke

The best-known routes don’t always provide the best discoveries. Museums that are difficult to pigeonhole are the ones that can make the biggest impression. Because of a special collection, a striking building or an unexpected combination of art, landscapes and history. Places like these invite you to linger and look around, without any set plan. You’ll find yourself pleasantly surprised, discover new connections and realise how a small detour can sometimes lead to the most extraordinary story of your journey.

Take a trip to Dordrecht to discover six centuries of Dutch paintings. At Singer Laren, you can see _The Thinker_, alongside refined black-and-white drawings and colourful paintings. Combine a visit to the Museum Beelden aan Zee with a refreshing walk on the beach at Scheveningen, followed by a coffee amongst the sculptures in the museum garden. In Drenthe, archaeology, art and landscapes come together in a surprising way. Various places offer art collections that defy conventional categories: quirky, diverse and well worth the detour, and always showcasing something new.

# The art of discovery \- Art Alliance in the Netherlands

© Stella Dekker Fotografie

Full screen Close

## The art of discovery

Create the most beautiful memories

Next

Some holiday memories just cannot be planned. They simply happen. A delightful pub garden in the afternoon sun. A walk that ends up being a little longer than planned. Or a spontaneous museum visit where you’re unexpectedly moved by a painting, a story or another encounter with art. Between a city walk, lunch by the water or an afternoon of shopping, a visit to a museum can easily become the highlight of the day.

32 million museum visits a year in the Netherlands

The element of surprise is exactly what makes travelling so special. Just like discovering a hidden lane, a local restaurant or a beautiful view that was not in the guidebook, you can also discover a museum that changes the way you see a city or region. Suddenly, you look differently at the façades around you, understand why a landscape looks the way it does, or notice details that had previously escaped you.

© Valerie Spanjers via Kröller-Müller Museum

### Art as an added extra

The Netherlands is home to many such discoveries. Not only in its major cities, but across the whole country. With this in mind, the Art Alliance brings together exceptional museums throughout the Netherlands. Not as a checklist of places to visit, but as a source of inspiration along the way.

Discover the [Rijksmuseum](https://www.rijksmuseum.nl/en 'https://www.rijksmuseum.nl/en')’s iconic art treasures, the combination of archaeology and art at the [Drents Museum](https://drentsmuseum.nl/en 'https://drentsmuseum.nl/en'), or the ever-changing exhibitions at [Kunsthal Rotterdam](https://www.kunsthal.nl/en/ 'https://www.kunsthal.nl/en/'). And what about the [Kröller-Müller Museum](https://www.krollermuller.nl/en?utm_source=web&utm_medium=link&utm_campaign=nbtc 'https://www.krollermuller.nl/en?utm_source=web&utm_medium=link&utm_campaign=nbtc') in the Veluwe, where nature and art come together, or [Singer Laren](https://www.singerlaren.nl/en?utm_source=Holland.com&utm_medium=display+ads&utm_campaign=Art+Alliantie+campagne 'https://www.singerlaren.nl/en?utm_source=Holland.com&utm_medium=display+ads&utm_campaign=Art+Alliantie+campagne'), where everyone can find a work of art that speaks to them.

© Daan Steijnen van Eck in Rijksmuseum

© Drents Museum Assen

© Museum Beelden aan Zee

The [Art Alliance museums](https://www.holland.com/global/tourism/getting-around/interests/art-alliance-museums 'The Art Alliance museums') invite you to discover the Netherlands through art, stories and encounters. From world-famous masterpieces to surprising contemporary art. From design and photography to history, heritage and remarkable collections in unexpected places. Wherever you find yourself, there’s always another discovery just around the corner.

© Ernst Wagensveld in Dordrechts Museum

Full screen Close

## Dutch Masters and icons

Face to face with masterpieces

Next

© Ernst Wagensveld in Frans Hals Museum

Some works of art are familiar before you ever see them in real life. You’ve seen them in books, on postcards or online. But nothing prepares you for the moment you stand face to face with one and can admire every single detail. Take the time to look closely and pause for a moment. Only then can you appreciate the miracle of light in a Vermeer, the vibrancy of a Frans Hals portrait, or how much emotion is contained in a brushstroke by Van Gogh.

### The country of Rembrandt, Vermeer and Frans Hals

© Ivo Hoektra via Mauritshuis Den Haag

Anyone wishing to understand the Netherlands soon discovers that art and history are inseparably connected here. The great masters tell stories of trade, faith, wealth, everyday life and the enduring relationship between water and landscape. Look beyond [Amsterdam](https://www.holland.com/global/tourism/visit-the-netherlands/visit-the-cities/amsterdam 'Amsterdam'), as Dutch Masters and iconic works of art can be found throughout the Netherlands.

In [The Hague](https://www.holland.com/global/tourism/visit-the-netherlands/visit-the-cities/the-hague 'The Hague'), the [Mauritshuis](https://www.mauritshuis.nl/en?utm_source=artalliantie&utm_medium=website&utm_campaign=dekunstvanhetontdekken&utm_id=landingspagina 'https://www.mauritshuis.nl/en?utm_source=artalliantie&utm_medium=website&utm_campaign=dekunstvanhetontdekken&utm_id=landingspagina') awaits with world-famous masterpieces that attract visitors from across the globe, while [Haarlem’s](https://www.holland.com/global/tourism/visit-the-netherlands/visit-the-cities/haarlem 'Haarlem') [Frans Hals Museum](https://franshalsmuseum.nl/en 'https://franshalsmuseum.nl/en') shows just how innovative portraiture can be. Remarkable encounters can also be found off the beaten track. In the historic centre of [Dordrecht](https://www.holland.com/global/tourism/visit-the-netherlands/visit-the-cities/dordrecht 'Dordrecht'), the [Dordrechts Museum](https://www.dordrechtsmuseum.nl/english/ 'https://www.dordrechtsmuseum.nl/english/') offers a wonderful journey through six centuries of Dutch painting. In the Veluwe National Park, visitors can combine a cycle ride through woods and heathland with a visit to one of the world’s largest Van Gogh collections at the [Kröller-Müller Museum](https://www.krollermuller.nl/en?utm_source=web&utm_medium=link&utm_campaign=nbtc 'https://www.krollermuller.nl/en?utm_source=web&utm_medium=link&utm_campaign=nbtc').

### Did you know..

that Haarlem-based Frans Hals inspired greats such as Manet, Monet and Van Gogh?

### A valuable addition to your trip

© Singer Laren Museum

It is exactly that remarkable combination that makes a trip special: start the day in nature, spend the afternoon surrounded by masterpieces, then settle down at a sunny terrace with a good glass of wine. Art is not to be seen separate from its surroundings, but becomes a natural part of everything you see and experience along the way.

And that is perhaps the greatest strength of the Dutch Masters: they teach you to look more closely. Not just at the light, colour and details in their paintings, but also at the Netherlands beyond the museum. At the clouds above the landscape, the quiet streets and everyday moments that can suddenly turn into something special.

© Iris van den Broek Depot Boijmans Van Beuningen in Rotterdam

Full screen Close

## Modern art and design

A new perspective on the world

Next

Modern art is usually not about recognition but about seeing things from a new perspective. Rather than giving answers, it poses questions. It experiments, provokes and encourages you to look differently at things that seem self-evident. That's exactly why contemporary art can feel so right while on holiday. You’re relaxed, have plenty of time and are receptive to new impressions.

© Marco De Swart

A holiday is the ideal time to be inspired by today’s artists and designers. With an open outlook and a relaxed frame of mind, creativity has room to flourish. Let your thoughts wander and be amazed by the expressive power of art. Contemporary works offer a new perspective on ourselves and the world, broadening your horizon. An encounter with art is a powerful source of energy that stays with you long after you return home.

© Aron Weidenaar via Fries Museum

### Cities buzzing with creative energy

The Netherlands enjoys global recognition for its designers and architects, who have filled its museums, and its streets as well. In [Rotterdam](https://www.holland.com/global/tourism/visit-the-netherlands/visit-the-cities/rotterdam 'Rotterdam') you can marvel at iconic buildings, modern skyline views and innovative urban development. Combine a visit to the [Depot of Museum Boijmans Van Beuningen](https://www.boijmans.nl/en/depot?utm_source=meta&utm_medium=cpc&utm_campaign=art_alliantie_2026&utm_content=%7B%7Bad.name%7D%7D 'https://www.boijmans.nl/en/depot?utm_source=meta&utm_medium=cpc&utm_campaign=art_alliantie_2026&utm_content=%7B%7Bad.name%7D%7D') with a bite to eat on the rooftop terrace of this striking building. Browse the Markthal, an icon in its own right, passing bookstalls and shops, then enjoy exotic music on lively terraces. Discover how art, design and everyday life naturally coexist in Rotterdam.

© Marco De Swart

The vibrant city of Rotterdam is full of surprises. Visiting [Kunsthal Rotterdam](https://www.kunsthal.nl/en/ 'https://www.kunsthal.nl/en/') is an interactive experience. You won't just be gazing at art, you'll experience it or may even become part of it. Located on the river Rhine, [Museum Arnhem](https://www.museumarnhem.nl/en 'https://www.museumarnhem.nl/en') combines art with spectacular views of the countryside. It is a place that naturally invites you to slow down for a moment. Set against the green backdrop of the surrounding area, design and fashion flourish here.

© Almicheal Fraay via Centraal Museum Utrecht

[Utrecht](https://www.holland.com/global/tourism/visit-the-netherlands/visit-the-cities/utrecht 'Utrecht'), too, is all about unexpected combinations. At the [Centraal Museum](https://www.centraalmuseum.nl/en 'https://www.centraalmuseum.nl/en'), Old Masters, fashion, design and contemporary art come together. Stroll past everything from intricately detailed dolls’ houses to catwalks. And of course, no visit would be complete without visiting the studio of Dick Bruna, the creator of Miffy.

Modern art invites you to pause and take a deep breath. To resist an easy explanation. That's precisely wherein its power lies. With a relaxed mind and no expectations, there is room for wonder. It's an encounter that brings fresh energy and often stays with you long after the holiday is over. Once back home, that fresh perspective can help you break out of familiar patterns and look at things differently.

© Jelle Draper

> A holiday is the ideal time to be inspired by today’s artists and designers.

© Stedelijk Museum Breda

© Eva Broekema via Museum Arnhem

Full screen Close

## Stories in their proper place

Discover heritage and history

Next

© Ernst Wagensveld in Westfries Museum

Stories bring destinations to life. Stroll past historic buildings and canals lined with boats, sit on a terrace overlooking the weigh house, the main church or the heart of the market square, and it’s easy to be struck by the beauty of it all. But once you understand what has happened there, what the story is behind these places, they take on even greater meaning.

Museums bring stories to life. In Hoorn, the [Westfries Museum](https://westfriesmuseum.nl/en?utm_source=hollandcom&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=art_alliantie_2026 'https://westfriesmuseum.nl/en?utm_source=hollandcom&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=art_alliantie_2026') shows how the Netherlands was connected to the world by water during the prosperous 17th century. Suddenly, the warehouses, harbours and grand façades you encounter in this town acquire more significance. In [Breda](https://www.holland.com/global/tourism/visit-the-netherlands/visit-the-cities/breda 'Breda'), the [Stedelijk Museum Breda](https://www.stedelijkmuseumbreda.nl/en 'https://www.stedelijkmuseumbreda.nl/en') offers a contemporary perspective on art and society, while also providing a glimpse into the history of the Dutch royal family.

### Stories of regions and people

Beyond the cities, the Netherlands also has distinct regions with their own identity, traditions and history. The [Limburgs Museum](https://www.limburgsmuseum.nl/en?utm_source=NBTC&utm_medium=website&utm_campaign=kliks_website_nbtc 'https://www.limburgsmuseum.nl/en?utm_source=NBTC&utm_medium=website&utm_campaign=kliks_website_nbtc') in Venlo, for example, tells how borders, migration and culture shape a region, something which remains surprisingly relevant to this day. The same is true in [Leeuwarden](https://www.holland.com/global/tourism/visit-the-netherlands/visit-the-cities/leeuwarden 'Leeuwarden'), where the [Fries Museum](https://www.friesmuseum.nl/en 'https://www.friesmuseum.nl/en') and [Princessehof Ceramics Museum](https://www.princessehof.nl/en 'https://www.princessehof.nl/en') show how regional stories, international art and ceramics enhance one another.

© Limburgs Museum

© Thomas Nondh Jansen via Keramiekmuseum Princessehof

### A personal experience

© Aron Weidenaar via Fries Museum

These museums show that heritage is not a collection of facts, but a living layer beneath every destination. That may be the most wonderful discovery of all. You came for an active holiday or a relaxed city break, but now you also understand what makes your chosen destination so special. Not because you’ve seen more, but because you’ve experienced more.

© Aad Hoogendoorn in Stedelijk Museum Breda, in de expo David Bade – We OK!

Full screen Close

## Off the beaten track

Surprising collections and destinations

Next

### An unforgettable holiday

Sometimes it’s the things you didn’t expect that stay with you the longest. A musical performance on a balmy summer evening. A museum tucked away in the woods. A walk on the beach that takes you to a museum by the sea. The impressive work of an artist you hadn’t heard of before. It's these unexpected discoveries that make a holiday unforgettable.

### Did you know?

The mirrored Depot is the first art storage facility in the world to open its doors to the public?

© Iris van den Broek at Depot Boijmans van Beuningen

### A little bit different

© Ankor Light at Museum Beelden aan Zee

Some museums do things just a little differently or are worth a detour. In Scheveningen, [Museum Beelden aan Zee](https://www.beeldenaanzee.nl/en 'https://www.beeldenaanzee.nl/en') offers a unique combination of beach walks, dunes and views of the North Sea. In places like these, the surroundings, the light, the breeze and the scents come together to create a holistic experience never to be forgotten.

In the north of the country, the [Drents Museum](https://drentsmuseum.nl/en 'https://drentsmuseum.nl/en') connects archaeology, art and age-old stories to the surrounding landscape. Make your visit even more memorable with a walk across the moor or a bike ride past the prehistoric dolmens. Along the way, you experience how history and culture come together here, while the ever-present stillness seems to invite you to stay a little longer and take an even closer look around.

### Art and heritage are everywhere

What a gift it is to look back at the end of a day on holiday and remember one of those unexpected moments of wonder. An artwork that moved you. A story that stuck with you. A museum that enhanced your trip. That’s the art of discovery!

© Margot Brakel Singer Laren

The Art Alliance won’t help you choose just one museum, but invites you to see the Netherlands anew, time and again. Through art, history, design and culture. Through familiar icons and unexpected finds. Wherever you begin, there's always another discovery awaiting you just around the corner.

[Discover the Art Alliance museums](https://www.holland.com/global/tourism/getting-around/interests/art-alliance-museums 'The Art Alliance museums')

© Erik Smits via Rijksmuseum

# current exhibitions

In 2026, HEART presents three very different exhibitions, each rooted in the museum’s unique collection and offering new perspectives on how art is created, collected, and experienced. 

**Form | Imprint** explores how the ideas of Concrete Art from the 1960s continue to resonate in contemporary artistic practice. Newly acquired works by Charlotte Brüel and Gun Gordillo are presented in dialogue with works by Gunnar Aagaard Andersen and Paul Gadegaard, activating the museum’s collection and highlighting artistic connections that emerge across time. 

**Bitten by the Bug** offers a fascinating insight into a number of private art collections in Jutland. Works from private collections are shown alongside artworks from HEART’s own collection, giving visitors a unique opportunity to explore the passion, curiosity, and dedication that drive art collectors. 

With **Everything is wrong**, visitors enter a playful and exploratory universe where art and everyday objects intertwine. Through this reinterpretation of Herning’s artistic and cultural history, new connections, perspectives, and stories emerge, inviting audiences to see familiar things in unexpected ways. 

### HEART - HERNING MUSEUM OF CONTEMPORARY ART

# Museum expansion

### The museum is temporarily closed due to renovation – but we will return even stronger in spring 2027.

For 14 months, Trapholt will be closed to visitors as the museum undergoes a major transformation. We’re expanding, renovating, and reimagining – with a focus on sustainability, improved accessibility, more opportunities, and even more space for communication and community. The vision is clear: Trapholt will be a cultural beacon and green haven that invites even more people to experience world-class art and design.

The renovation doesn’t mean we’re disappearing – quite the opposite. During this period, we’ll be present throughout Kolding with Trapholt To Go, workshops, school projects, and events. Trapholt comes to you while we build the museum of the future.

## FAQ

Vis mere Vis mindre

**When does the renovation start, and how long will the museum be closed?**

The renovation will begin on January 1, 2026. The last day the museum is open to the public will be December 30, 2025, and we expect to reopen on March 1, 2027. You can already look forward to a big reopening celebration!

**Why is the museum closing completely – can’t it remain partially open?**

The renovation affects large parts of both the interior and exterior of the museum, making it impossible to ensure a safe and high-quality experience for visitors during the work. A complete closure is necessary to carry out the project efficiently and safely.

**What can we look forward to afterward?**

Trapholt will have more space and improved facilities to match the growing number of visitors and our high ambitions for communication and guest experience. Among the new features will be:

- A new CRAFT/learning center with flexible spaces that can be adapted for everything from children’s workshops to large conferences and lectures with up to 500 participants.

- A new sculpture lounge adjacent to the guest reception area – a gathering place for people and significant artworks, featuring glass panels that open the museum toward the park and surrounding nature.

- An upgraded park area with new pathways, art installations, scenic viewpoints, and relaxation spots that invite all visitors – regardless of mobility – to enjoy the interplay between art and nature.

**Is sustainability considered in the project?**

Yes – sustainability is a key guiding principle for the entire project. Trapholt aims to be a role model for sustainable museum construction of the future, working with four dimensions of sustainability:

- **Social**: The building must be inclusive and accessible to everyone – both physically and mentally.

- **Cultural**: Respect for Trapholt’s existing architecture and C.Th. Sørensen’s historic park is fundamental.

- **Environmental**: Requirements include low CO2 emissions, use of eco-labeled materials, and life cycle assessments (LCA) from the architectural competition stage.

- **Economic**: The building is designed with high flexibility, ensuring that the space can be used for various purposes and support sustainable operation.

**What is the renovation process?**

The renovation of Trapholt began with an architectural competition, announced as an EU public tender with prior prequalification. This ensures that the project complies with EU regulations for public construction and guarantees an open, transparent, and fair competition.

Five interdisciplinary teams – consisting of architects, landscape architects, engineers, and sustainability specialists – have been selected to participate. Each team is developing a comprehensive and visionary proposal that meets Trapholt’s functional needs and sets a new standard for sustainable and inclusive architecture. The winner was selected at the end of April 2025, and the winning proposal is the basis for the continued development of the project. See more further down this page.

**What will happen to Trapholt’s staff during the closure?**

Even though the building will be closed, the museum will still be active. We’ll continue to work on future exhibitions and everything else that typically happens behind the scenes. Additionally, through the projects _Trapholt To Go_ and _Trapholt Pop Up_, we’ll move out into Kolding Municipality with art projects, events, and educational programs. We’ll visit schools, take part in city events, and bring the Trapholt spirit into new spaces – we look forward to meeting you out there!

**What will happen to Café Gustav Lind?**

Café Gustav Lind will close along with the rest of the museum. Already planned and pre-booked events will, of course, proceed as scheduled. 
Restaurateur Rasmus Vemmelund is also working on exciting new ventures elsewhere in the city – more on that soon. 
If you have questions about the café, feel free to contact Rasmus directly at: Rasmus@gustavlind.dk

**How can I stay updated on the project?**

We’ll regularly update this page, but you are also very welcome to sign up for our newsletter via this link.

**Still have questions?**

Please don’t hesitate to write to us at: kunstmuseum@trapholt.dk – we’re happy to help!

## Selected Illustrations

The winner of the architectural competition was 3XN. The winning project includes an expanded guest reception area, the creation of a sculpture lounge, a flexible learning and CRAFT center, as well as a new, integrated experience of the museum’s unique park landscape. # Exhibitions

Le Petit Palais présente tout au long de l’année de grandes expositions temporaires, mêlant chefs-d’œuvre, découvertes et dialogues entre les arts. Ces rendez-vous offrent un regard renouvelé sur l’histoire de l’art et les artistes qui l’ont façonnée, en écho aux collections permanentes du musée.

Aucune exposition en cours ou à venir.

## Pour aller plus loin

### Les expositions passées

Retrouvez toutes les expositions temporaires présentées au Petit Palais depuis 2008.

[Les expositions passées](https://www.petitpalais.paris.fr/en/discover-programme/expositions/past-exhibitions)

Pekka Halonen, _Paysage d’hiver, Myllykylä_, 1896. Ateneum Art Museum. Crédit : Finnish National Gallery / Aleks Talve

### Les expositions virtuelles

Le portail des collections des musées de la Ville de Paris propose plusieurs expositions virtuelles et parcours thématiques valorisant notamment les collections d'arts graphiques du Petit Palais.

[En savoir plus sur les expositions et les parcours en ligne](https://www.petitpalais.paris.fr/en/node/120)

@graph.description: Museum Dhondt-Dhaenens is an internationally regarded museum of contemporary and modern art. The Museum is part of Stichting Mevrouw Jules Dhondt-Dhaenens, a Flemish private foundation founded in Deurle in 1967 by Jules and Irma Dhondt-Dhaenens. The Foundation upholds the Dhondt-Dhaenens’ original vision to make their art collection, as well as culture more broadly, accessible to diverse audiences in Flanders, Belgium and internationally. Alongside Museum Dhondt-Dhaenens, the Stichting Mevrouw Jules Dhondt-Dhaenens encompasses two associated sites, the Wunderkammer and Woning Van Wassenhove.

## TOWERMMK

Since 2014, the MUSEUMMMKFÜR MODERNE KUNST has had a third venue, TOWERMMK, which is located in the city centre not far from the station district and the museum’s main building.

The exhibition space of around 2,000 square metres was made available to the MUSEUMMMKFÜR MODERNE KUNST by Tishman Speyer. The founding partners are Stefan Quandt, the Ernst Max von Grunelius-Stiftung, DekaBank Deutsche Girozentrale and Helaba Landesbank Hessen-Thüringen. Further sponsors are the MMK Stiftung, the Freunde des MMK and the New Contemporaries.

### Venue Information

##### TOWERMMK

TaunusTurm, Taunustor 1 
60310 Frankfurt am Main

[+49 69 212 73165](tel:+496921273165) 
[mmk@stadt-frankfurt.de](mailto:tower@mmk.art)

- MondayClosed

ZOLLAMTMMK + TOWERMMK COMBINED TICKET 
11 € / 5 € 

TOWERMMK TICKET  
8 € / 4 €

Reduced admission: school pupils, students, vocational trainees, the unemployed, the severely handicapped, Frankfurt Card holders, groups of 20 or more

As part of the SaTOURday, admission to the MUSEUMMMKFÜR MODERNE KUNST is free every last Saturday of the month. On numerous dates there are also free thematic guided tours for families.

Admission free for: [FRIENDS OF THE MMK](https://www.mmk.art/de/about/friends-of-mmk/), children and teenagers under 18, ICOM (International Council of Museums) Card holders, [Museumsufer Card](https://www.museumsufercard.de/#) holders, students of the Goethe University Frankfurt am Main, the Städelschule, the Hochschule für Gestaltung Offenbach, the Hochschule für Musik und Darstellende Kunst and the University of Applied Sciences Frankfurt, teachers accompanying a school class and refugees. 
Please present the respective documents of proof at the museum cashier’s desk.

Other discounts: Holders of the Frankfurt Pass pay a reduced admission fee of 1 € at all three MUSEUMMMK FÜR MODERNE KUNST venues. Please present the respective documents of proof at the museum cashier’s desk.

ALSO AVAILABLE AT THE MUSEUM CASHIER’S DESK

### Education

[Art education](https://www.mmk.art/en/learning-and-research/education) is making the MMK a place for collective thinking, exchange, experimentation, questioning and understanding. We try to create an appropriate temporality and place for many people to collect diverse perspectives and opinions, to make them visible and audible.

In this process, we keep the needs of a changing society in mind and work together with art and cultural actors, organisations, colleges/universities, museums, day-care centres and schools – to try out something different and to develop new knowledge and expertise.

You can find all public events [here](https://www.mmk.art/en/whats-on).

Registration, information, guided tour or workshop booking: 
+49 69 212 40691 (Mon, Tue, Thu 8 am–1 pm; Wed 3–8 pm) 
[kunstvermittlung.mmk@stadt-frankfurt.de](mailto:kunstvermittlung.mmk@stadt-frankfurt.de)

### Accessibility

Access to the TOWERMMK is barrier-free. There is an elevator in the TOWERMMK. Barrier-free restrooms are located on the ground floor and the 2nd floor. Stools are available at the entrance to the exhibition.

### MMK begleitet

Duration: max. 2 hours 
Cost: included in the admission fee 
In German

For everyone who wants individual and empathetic support, we offer personal one-on-one visits to the exhibitions. Together with a mediator from our education team, you will experience art in a personalized way and own individual interests and needs to the visit.

You decide which works you would like to learn more about, how detailed the image descriptions should be—live audio description is also available—and which topics appeal to you most.

The tour starts by arrangement in the foyer or in front of the building. You can also be picked up at the underground, bus or tram station or at the taxi stand.

Developed in collaboration with Lilian Korner (blind cultural scientist and inclusion activist), Martina Reuter (audio description for film/television/theater), and a testing group from the _Frankfurt Foundation for the Blind and Visually Impaired_.

Appointments by arrangement. Give us a call or write to us to discuss your interests and specific needs in advance.

As appointments are made on an individual basis, we kindly ask you to register in advance at: [kunstvermittlung.mmk@stadt-frankfurt.de](mailto:kunstvermittlung.mmk@stadt-frankfurt.de) or +49 69 212 40691 (Mon–Thu, 9 am–2 pm).

### Lockers

Valuables can be stored in lockers. 
Portable stools are available free of charge.

### Elaine's Deli at the TOWERMMK

Elaine's Deli, the TOWERMMK museum café, offers small dishes as well as coffee specialities. In good weather, the large sun terrace is open.

# Along the Color Line – Traces of a Transatlantic Modernism

### October 3, 2026 – March 7, 2027

**To mark its 50th anniversary, the Museum Ludwig is staging a major interdisciplinary survey exhibition that explores the connections between the art of the international Black diaspora and European modernism. The exhibition features modernist and contemporary works by artists of the Black diaspora through a host of international loans that are presented in dialogue with pieces from the Museum Ludwig collection. These works include paintings, sculptures, drawings, literature, and music, highlighting the diversity of artistic expression that served as a platform for cultural exchange and engagement at the beginning of the twentieth century.**

The title of the exhibition is borrowed from the writings of the African American sociologist W. E. B. Du Bois. Having studied in Berlin, in 1936, while working as a journalist for _The__Pittsburgh Courier_, Du Bois visited several German cities, including Cologne, Hamburg, and Stuttgart, and attended the Wagner Festival in Bayreuth and the Olympic Games in Berlin. His academic work offers a unique testimony of this period in history, enhancing our understanding of the global interconnections between racism and exclusion. In the exhibition, Du Bois’s reports are accompanied by accounts from other prominent figures of the Black diaspora in Europe, including the philosopher Alain Locke (1885–1954). Locke taught at Howard University, which has generously loaned items from its collection, where his academic writings and collection of international art are housed today.

The exhibition’s line of enquiry stems from a study of the Museum Ludwig collection, which revealed, as in most European museums, a virtual absence of works by Black artists, particularly in the realm of modernism. This underrepresentation points to deep-rooted colonial and social power dynamics whose effects are still evident today. With this context in mind, the exhibition explores how Black artists used their works to create new narratives that challenged colonial and Eurocentric habits of seeing. By drawing on movements such as the Harlem Renaissance in the United States and the Négritude movement in Europe, the exhibition traces the artistic relations between both continents and their influence on artists working today.

An important focus of the exhibition is the work of the German American artist James Gregory Atkinson (\*1981). His nonlinear archive of images, objects, writings, and oral histories, which engages with African American history and bears witness to the history of Black people in Germany, serves as a central work in the show, linking early twentieth-century movements to current Black diasporic experiences.

Works by artists of the Black diaspora who spent time in Europe and the Rhine region show how questions of migration, identity, and cultural belonging are just as much local concerns as they are global ones. The works of Mildred Thompson, for example, who lived in Düren in the 1960s and studied at Howard University, provide the exhibition with a strong local emphasis.

In the run-up to the exhibition, the Museum Ludwig purchased a number of works by Thompson, Herbert Gentry (1919–2003), and Iba Ndiaye (1928–2008). Through their transnational biographies and aesthetic positions, these artists offer new perspectives on (post)modernism. _Along the Color Line_ opens up a dialogue between the museum’s holdings, these new acquisitions, and international loans, revealing previously hidden intercultural ties and transatlantic connections running through the core themes of the Museum Ludwig collection: European modernism and American postmodernism.

More than a century after W. E. B. Du Bois and Alain Locke traveled through modern-day Germany and Europe, this exhibition invites visitors to reflect on the social significance of cultural identity, community, and belonging and to consider the importance of creative solutions for living with and between different cultures—both then and now.

➤ **You can find the exhibition booklet here:** [**in English**](https://www.museum-ludwig.de/fileadmin/content/00_Ausstellungen/_Medien/2026/Along_the_Color_Line/ML-ATCL-BHEN-FIN-3.pdf) **/** [**in German**](https://www.museum-ludwig.de/fileadmin/content/00_Ausstellungen/_Medien/2026/Along_the_Color_Line/Begleitheft_deutsch.pdf)

**Curator:** Eboa Itondo  
**Project assistant:** Alison Shea

The exhibition is funded by the Ministry of Culture and Science of the State of North Rhine-Westphalia, the Kulturstiftung des Bundes (German Federal Cultural Foundation). Funded by the Beauftragte der Bundesregierung für Kultur und Medien (Federal Government Commissioner for Culture and the Media), the Kunststiftung NRW, and the Terra Foundation for American Art. It is also supported by the Peter and Irene Ludwig Foundation, the Friends of the Wallraf-Richartz Museum and the Museum Ludwig e.V., the Cultural Foundation of the German States, and the Beatrix Lichtken Foundation. The exhibition is sponsored by the REWE Group.

metadata.description: To mark its 50th anniversary, the Museum Ludwig is staging a major interdisciplinary survey exhibition that explores the connections between the art of the international Black diaspora and European modernism. The exhibition features modernist and contemporary works by artists of the Black diaspora through a host of international loans that are presented in dialogue with pieces from the Museum Ludwig collection. These works include paintings, sculptures, drawings, literature, and music, highlighting the diversity of artistic expression that served as a platform for cultural exchange and engagement at the beginning of the twentieth century.

## Chartered buses / groups

Entry and exit is possible in the immediate vicinity of the museum. Bus parking spaces are located on the banks of the Tonhalle.

## Transfer K20 / K21

FAQ

## Webshop

### Do you offer time slot tickets?

No timed-entry tickets are required for the permanent collections at K20 and K21 or for most special exhibitions. Time-slot tickets are required for “Playground”. 

All admission tickets (except time-slot tickets and special offer tickets) are valid for one year from the date of purchase and entitle the holder to one admission to K20 or K21. The tickets will be sent to you separately by e-mail as a PDF after the booking confirmation.

We accept digital and printed tickets. Due to different visitor flows, there may sometimes be waiting times even with an online ticket.

### What conditions apply to online tickets?

At our Webshop, you can purchase online tickets for visits to the K20 and the K21. Tickets are valid for 1 year after the sale date. 

Once payment has been received, online tickets are sent as e-mail attachments (PDF). Delivery by mail is not possible. 

Please be sure the barcode on your printed ticket is legible and undamaged.

### Do I need a user account?

You can register at our Webshop, or complete the order process as a guest. Available currently is payment via credit card (VISA for Master Card). Payments via invoice is not possible.

### Can I exchange a ticket or product purchase at the Webshop?

Online tickets and tickets for events booked at the Webshop cannot be exchanged or refunded. 

Valid for all other articles ordered from the Webshop (exhibition catalogs, for example) is the statutory cancellation deadline of 14 days, provided products are returned this period. In such instances, the purchase price will be refunded. This is the case as well for damaged or defective products.  

For technical reasons, it is not possible to cancel an order from the Webshop.

### Questions about an order or the shipment of an article

For general questions, please contact our visitor’s service; in specific cases, contact our Sales Department at [service@kunstsammlung.de](mailto:service@kunstsammlung.de).

## Cloakrooms, lockers and belongings

### What do I do with jackets, bags, and suitcases (bulky objects)?

We kindly ask you to leave coats, large bags and bulky or wet items at the cloakroom or deposited in one of the lockers. Please check or leave your jacket as well. 

In both museums, cloakrooms and lockers (free of charge) are found in the entrance areas.

### Who do I contact if I have lost or forgotten my belongings?

As a rule, objects lost in the museum are surrendered to the ticket counter. Staffmembers will then deposit these objects with the security center.  

After a period of time, lost objects are handed over to the lost property office. In the event you have left objects behind in the locked locker, you may retrieve them on the following day during museum hours.

## During your visit

### Can I take photographs, sketch, or paint in the museum?

Taking photographs for private purposes is permitted in the exhibition galleries. For reasons of copyright protection, we may prohibit the taking of photographs in special exhibitions, or in front of specific works. The corresponding notices will be posted on site. 

Taking photographs or filming for commercial purposes of any kind is permissible only with prior written agreement (filming permit).

Sketchpads in DIN A3 format, as well as pencils, may be brought into the exhibition galleries.

### Conduct in the museum: telephoning, eating, drinking?

Please understand that telephoning in the museum is undesirable. Eating and drinking, as well as smoking, is not permitted in the exhibition galleries. 

Parents, legal guardians, and group leaders are responsible for the appropriate conduct of the children and young people in their charge. 

The primary task of the supervisory staff is to protect the exhibit objects from damage.

### Are there seating options?

Folding chairs can be borrowed from the cloakroom free of charge, and can be taken into the exhibition galleries.

## Accessibility

### Are the museums accessible?

The K20 and the K21 are accessible for the most part.

### Is preferential admittance possible for individuals with disabilities?

In the event of queues or longer waiting times, bearers of an official disabled persons pass will receive preferential admittance.

### What about wheelchairs and walkers?

Visitors with walking impairments may borrow wheelchairs from the cloakroom free of charge for the duration of the visit (if possible, with prior registration with the visitor’s service). 

Also available at the cloakroom (also without prior registration) are folding chairs that can be used as walkers.

### Can I bring my service dog?

With the proper credentials, seeing eye dogs and service dogs for disabled individuals can be brought into the museum. 

Chaperones for blind or visually impaired visitors pay no admission charge.

## General terms and conditions

### Where can praise, complaints, or suggestions be registered

Our visitor’s service is happy to receive feedback of all kinds. 

Please use our contact form, or send an e-mail to service@kunstsammlung.de

### Is public Wi-Fi available?

Offered in the public areas of the K20 and the K21 is cost-free Internet access: Wi-Fi hotspots are located in the entrance area, in the Trinkaus Auditorium, in the library, and in the Salon20 in the K20 and the piazza and Salon21 in the K21. 

Please use your web-enabled terminal device to connect to the networks “K20 public” and “K21 public” and accept the general conditions for the Internet access service of the Kunstsammlung Nordrhein-Westfalen.

### Where do I find the general terms and conditions (GTC)?

You can find the​ GTC of the Kunstsammlung Nordrhein-Westfalen in the imprint of this Internet page.

### Where can I find the house regulations?

The house regulatio​ns of the Kunstsammlung Nordrhein-Westfalen are displayed at the ticket counters of the K20 and the K21.

## RENOVATION

The City of Frankfurt is continuing the extensive fire safety renovation of the listed MUSEUMMMKFÜR MODERNE KUNST building. The City of Frankfurt´s Office for Construction and Real Estate is carrying out the work on behalf of the Department of Culture.

According to the current schedule, the renovation is expected to be completed in the beginning of 2027. An exact date has not yet been confirmed. We will provide an update here as soon as further information becomes available.

As the renovation work cannot be carried out while the museum is open to the public, the MUSEUMMMK will remain closed during the work. However, the foyer and the MUSEUMMMK bookstore will remain accessible.

We look forward to welcoming you to TOWERMMK and ZOLLAMTMMK in the meantime. Both locations remain open to visitors as usual.

# Special exhibitions

Several times a year, Kunstmuseum Moritzburg Halle (Saale) presents temporary exhibitions aimed at a national and international audience, as well as regional themes and artists. Again and again, outstanding items from the museum’s own collections are exhibited and put on show so as to illustrate different themes.

# **Ruth Campau · COLOR PUSH**

**September 26 2026 – February 21 2027**

Ruth Campau is a painter who works in an expanded field. Her painting is spatial, and she challenges painting’s standard systems. She often uses a broom instead of a brush, and she applies long and parallel paint strokes to transparent sheets of mirrors or acryl. Color is her primary remedy, and the stroke itself becomes the artistic ‘content’.

Welcome to Groninger Museum, the largest museum in the north of the Netherlands, for art and design.

Groninger Museum 
Museumeiland 1 
9711 ME Groningen

## Opening Hours

Tuesday to Sunday 10 am–5 pm 
Monday closed 

Groninger Museum is closed on 
Friday 18 September 
Friday 25 December (Christmas Day) 
Friday 1 January (New Year’s Day)

Photo: Nikola Lamburov

The Museum seen from the Groningen Central Station by Alessandro Mendini, 1989 © Groninger Museum, Photo: John Stoel

Photo: Kathrin Sonntag

## Admission prices

- Adults € 19.50
- Students & CJP € 10.00 

- Free admission: 
 Children up to and including 18 years old 
 Groninger Museum Salon 
 ICOM card

 Rembrandtkaart

## Visiting with a Group

Register your group by emailing [boekingen@groningermuseum.nl](mailto:boekingen@groningermuseum.nl). Registration is mandatory for all groups. Please ensure that your group has sufficient supervision at all times.

## By Train

The museum is approximately 300 metres from Groningen Central Station.

## By Car

By car take the A7 or A28 (via Zwolle) and, from Europaplein, follow the signs for the city centre. See [here](https://www.groningenbereikbaar.nl/) for the latest traffic situation in and around Groningen. For up-to-date information about parking in Groningen, it is best to check [VisitGroningen](https://www.visitgroningen.nl/nl/plan-je-bezoek/vervoer/parkeren). You can choose a Q-Park car park in the city centre or a P+R site on the outskirts of the city (park affordably and continue by public transport). The nearest Q-Park car park is Q-Park Museum Centrum.

Motorists with a disabled parking permit can park in one of the two disabled parking spaces on Ubbo Emmiussingel, adjacent to the museum.

Travelling into the city centre by company car? 
A zero-emission zone has been in effect since 1 April 2025. Find out more at [Groningen goes zero emissions](https://groningendoethetzero.nl/).

## By Bicycle

You can park your bike on the Ubbo Emmiussingel, in the racks along the water or in the bicycle storage facility at the Stadsbalkon by Groningen Central Station.

We look forward to welcoming you at the Groninger Museum. Prepare for your visit by ordering your ticket online beforehand, and discover more about our current programme, the building and the history of the museum here.

menu

close

# Visit

At The Nordic Watercolour Museum, you can view exhibitions from around the world, attend exciting events, experiment with colour and enjoy delicious dining. Come and experience encounters between nature, art and people.

[Opening hours & admission](https://www.akvarellmuseet.org/en/visit/hours-and-admission) [Find us](https://www.akvarellmuseet.org/en/visit/find-us)

The small coastal town of Skärhamn on the island of Tjörn is home to The Nordic Watercolour Museum. It attracts visitors from all continents – keen to experience contemporary art and the history of watercolour. The cultural offering makes this a vibrant location all year round and the museum is open throughout the seasons (except when closed for change-over of exhibitions). Thanks to its unique location right by the water’s edge, visitors to the museum can combine art experiences with a dip from the jetty. Welcome to The Nordic Watercolour Museum!

We always offer the chance for in-depth exploration of our exhibitions. Depending on the time of year, you can, for example, join a guided tour, take home a free booklet about the art or listen to an audio guide on your phone. We often produce films about our exhibitions and you can view these on both the website and [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/NordiskaAkvarellmuseet).

The Nordic Watercolour Museum is a place for all people and all ages. Bring the whole family and discover everything the museum has to offer. A number of our events are aimed at families and younger visitors, and these vary depending on the period. Perhaps you are interested in painting, guided tours or a performance? In addition, the museum has plenty of spots where you can sit for a while, to draw, read or discuss what you have seen. And why not refuel with some delicious cake in the café?

## Museum shop

The museum shop stocks a carefully selected range of watercolour materials, literature, crafts and Nordic design items. The assortment varies, in keeping with the current exhibition and the season. There is always an exciting selection to browse, for both adults and children.

Photo: AmplifyPhoto

## Workshop

Both children and adults can try their hand at watercolour art in our open studio, with watercolour materials and staff on hand to offer help if needed. Themed workshops take place during school holidays, with extended opening hours and free admission. Keep an eye on our events page to check opening hours and current information.

[Events at the museum](https://www.akvarellmuseet.org/en/events)

## Upper floor

Upstairs, the atmosphere is usually a little calmer. Here you will find Konstpausen, an area offering space and materials to try out watercolour pencils and drawing. You will also find Thordénrummet, a varied space, most often used as an exhibition area or for a variety of activities. The upper floor also houses Experimentverkstaden, which is used for courses and as a workshop for pre-booked groups.

## Restaurant & Café

The museum has its own eatery: Vatten Restaurang & Kafé. You can enjoy a bite to eat or a refreshing drink all year round. You are in for a memorable experience, amidst breathtaking scenery and served by a team that aim to deliver meals made from the best seasonal ingredients.

[Vatten Restaurang & Kafé](https://www.akvarellmuseet.org/en/visit/eat)

- [**Opening hours & admission**](https://www.akvarellmuseet.org/en/visit/hours-and-admission)

- [**Find us**](https://www.akvarellmuseet.org/en/visit/find-us)

- [**Guest studios**](https://www.akvarellmuseet.org/en/visit/gueststudios)

- [**Eat**](https://www.akvarellmuseet.org/en/visit/eat)

- [**Accessibility**](https://www.akvarellmuseet.org/en/visit/accessibility)

- [**School**](https://www.akvarellmuseet.org/en/school)

## discover the area

When the museum is closed, you can enjoy some outdoor **art**. _The Lighthouse_ is a cylindrical sculpture six metres in height by artist duo [Wolfgang Winter and Berthold Hörbelt](https://www.akvarellmuseet.org/en/the-collection/artists/berthold-hoerbelt-and-wolfgang-winter-en). It sits on a rocky islet right beside The Nordic Watercolour Museum; at night, it is illuminated, and inside is a bench. [Gunilla Hansson](https://www.akvarellmuseet.org/en/the-collection/artists/gunilla-hansson-en)’s installation _Singing Inhabitants_ runs along the deck surrounding the museum. The inscribed text tells of an atoll in the Pacific Ocean that is at risk of being swamped by rising sea levels.

The museum is located next to **Gråskärsbadet**, one of Tjörn’s largest bathing areas. It has a sandy beach, a diving platform, a beach volleyball court and public toilets. Above the bathing area stands _Hulda_, a sculpture by artist Linn Granlund owned by [Tjörn Municipality](https://www.tjorn.se/kultur-fritid-och-turism/konst-och-kultur/bild-och-form/offentlig-konst-pa-tjorn). 

Tjörn is also home to **Sculpture in Pilane**: a sculpture park and eight-hectare cultural landscape. The exhibition area is not a traditional park but a living landscape with grazing sheep, where you can wander freely or follow well-trodden paths over meadows and rocky outcrops. The rocky summits afford outstanding views of the North Sea and the Bohuslän archipelago. A 12-km hiking and cycling trail runs between The Nordic Watercolour Museum and [Pilane](https://pilane.org/en/index.php), through one of Sweden’s most scenic cultural landscapes. [More information](https://www.vastsverige.com/en/tjorn/trails/walking-and-cycling-between-nordic-watercolour-museum-and-pilane-sculpture-park/).

Tjörn is an island filled with culture and discoveries to be made. **Sundsby säteri** is a mythical manor dating from the 14th century, now housing a café, shops, a kitchen garden and hiking trails. You will also find a 5-km hiking trail around the picturesque island of **Dyrön**, which can be reached by ferry. You can choose to get off the ferry on the car-free island of **Åstol**, with its boathouses and leafy alleys, as well as a bathing area with a slide. On the far horizon, barren and windswept, towers the world-famous 32-metre-high **Pater Noster** lighthouse from 1868 – a state-of-the-art masterpiece in its day and now an award-winning design hotel. Tjörn is also home to a number of **farm shops, local handicraft studios** and **flea markets**. The island offer a multitude of [events](https://www.vastsverige.com/tjorn/evenemang/) all year round, and you can take your pick from fun, experimental and evocative experiences. Come and discover Tjörn, for an enriching encounter.

In the center of Borås, in the city's Culture House, is Borås Art Museum located – one of Sweden's largest museums for contemporary art outside the metropolitan regions. Free admission to all exhibitions and programs.

Photo: Hendrik Zeitler

# Opening hours

From 29 September to 29 November, the museum is in preparation for upcoming exhibitions. Please see the [Exhibition](https://boraskonstmuseum.se/english/boras-museum-of-modern-art/exhibitions.html)s section for information about exhibitions open to visitors during this period.

Kulturhuset 
P A Halls Terrass 
504 56 Borås

The nearest bus stop is "Bäckängsskolan." You can get there by taking bus lines 1, 3, 5, and 8.

Parking:The nearest parking is located between Kulturhuset and Bäckängsgymnasiet.

## Tours

Borås Art Museum has free admission, and our regular tours and introductions at the museum are free of charge. For private group tours, see the information below.

**Book a group tour**

View our current exhibitions or take a guided tour around Borås to see sculptures and urban art.

Contact us to customize your visit, for example with a meal at Utbult, the restaurant in Kulturhuset.

Costs: Booked tours for private groups

Tour (40-60 minutes) 1000 SEK 
Evening tour (after 5 PM) and weekends 1500 SEK

Bookings are only accepted via email: [bokningar.konstmuseum@boras.se](mailto:bokningar.konstmuseum@boras.se)

Photo: Hendrik Zeitler

## Restaurant

In Kulturhuset, right next to the museum, you'll find the restaurant Utbult Borneby & Co, which offers a bistro and café menu.

[Link to Utbult Borneby & Co (new window) Länk till annan webbplats, öppnas i nytt fönster.](https://www.utbultbornebyco.com/)

## Accessibility

Before Your Visit:

Transportation service (färdtjänst): Transportation services drop off passengers right at the entrance of Kulturhuset.

Pets: Guide and assistance dogs are allowed, but please inform the entrance staff so they are aware of the presence of pets in the museum.

Wheelchairs: If needed, there is a wheelchair available for loan. Please ask for assistance at the entrance.

Storage Facilities: On the basement level, there are coat hangers and free lockers available. Inform the entrance staff if you need to use the lockers.

Restrooms: There are restrooms on every floor of the museum. One to the right in the entrance, one upstairs, and several on the basement level, as well as in the studio. The restroom at the entrance is accessible.

Changing Table: The restroom near the entrance is equipped with a changing table.

Food and Drink: Eating or drinking brought-in food is not allowed in the museum premises, but please feel free to visit the restaurant in Kulturhuset.

On site:

Elevators: There is an elevator and stairs at the entrance that take you to the exhibitions on the second floor, as well as down to the cloakroom in the basement.

Seating: There are available seating areas on all floors throughout the museum. In the entrance, there are foldable chairs that you can carry with you during your visit. The number of seats and their placement may vary depending on the exhibition.

Language: Our staff speaks Swedish and English, and we offer guided tours in these languages.

Sign Language and Audio Description: Please contact the museum in advance if you need help arranging sign language or audio description services.

**Tillgänglighetsdatabasen** (Accessibility Database): This is a database that provides information on the physical accessibility of various places for your everyday visits to public services, stores, restaurants, outdoor areas, and other destinations.

# Centre Pompidou is transforming itself

Centre Pompidou 2030 - Laurent Le Bon, President of Centre Pompidou, Paris

In 2025, Centre Pompidou is beginning a major transformation.

■ In autumn 2025, its iconic Parisian building will close for renovation works aimed at reconnecting, by 2030, with its original utopian vision.

■ Meanwhile, the spirit of Centre Pompidou will resonate through numerous partner venues across France and internationally, thanks to its ambitious cultural program "Constellation".

■ In spring 2027, a new hub for conservation, exhibition and creation will open in Massy, Essonne: Centre Pompidou Francilien – fabrique de l’art.

- [The renovation project](https://www.centrepompidou.fr/en/centre-pompidou-is-transforming-itself#40153 'Centre Pompidou 2030')
|- [Constellation program 2025-2030](https://www.centrepompidou.fr/en/centre-pompidou-is-transforming-itself#31906 'Constellation program 2025-2030')
|- [Centre Pompidou Francilien](https://www.centrepompidou.fr/en/centre-pompidou-is-transforming-itself#31909 'Centre Pompidou Francilien – fabrique de l’art opens in 2027')

## Centre Pompidou 2030

### Reinventing Centre Pompidou’s original utopia

Following the gradual closure of all levels of the historic Beaubourg building, the major renovation project—entrusted to the architectural firms AIA Life Designers (technical component) and Moreau Kusunoki (cultural component), in collaboration with Frida Escobedo Studio—will begin in early 2026.

This undertaking combines technical and environmental components, such as the complete asbestos removal from the façade, treatment of corrosion on the main structure, renovation and energy optimization of the building, and improvements to accessibility. It also encompasses cultural aspects: enhancing the visitor experience, rethinking the display of the collection and the layout of the Bpi (Public Information Library), reconfiguring spatial organization to allow for greater emphasis on creation, and thereby reaffirming Centre Pompidou’s multidisciplinary identity.

Reimagined as a living space more deeply integrated into the urban fabric, Centre Pompidou will, in 2030, renew its invitation to society as a whole—more open and more committed than ever.

 [An iconic architecture](https://www.centrepompidou.fr/en/centre-pompidou-is-transforming-itself/an-iconic-architecture)

 [Renovation project Centre Pompidou 2030](https://www.centrepompidou.fr/en/centre-pompidou-is-transforming-itself/renovation-project-centre-pompidou-2030)

---

### Constellation program 2025-2030

#### A Centre Pompidou more vibrant than ever!

Although the renovation work on Centre Pompidou will not officially begin until early 2026, its spaces will gradually close to the public throughout 2025 to allow the teams to relocate under the best possible conditions. The building will close its doors on 22 September 2025 and offers one final festive event within its walls on 24 and 25 October 2025, [Because Beabourg](https://www.centrepompidou.fr/en/because-beaubourg).

#### Beginning in April 2025, the Constellation program will be launched.

Centre Pompidou is embracing this unprecedented moment to send its collection and multidisciplinary programming on the road, sharing its richness and expertise throughout France and around the world.

Far from placing the national collection into dormancy, the aim is quite the opposite: to make it more visible and accessible to the widest possible audience, while strengthening a long-standing policy of lending artworks and exhibitions. Just like the first exhibitions of the Constellation program–"Pom Pom Pidou" at Le Tripostal in Lille, "Dimanche sans fin. Maurizio Cattelan and Centre Pompidou Collection" at Centre Pompidou-Metz, and "Couleurs!" at the Grimaldi Forum in Monaco–the program offers new and exciting perspectives on the collection. It also allows Centre Pompidou’s dynamic, multidisciplinary programming to continue in many locations–live performances, cinema, and spoken word, along with its outreach and educational activities. Constellation is built on friendly and reciprocal partnerships with institutions–including Centre Pompidou-Metz, the Grand Palais, and soon Centre Pompidou Francilien–, cities, and regions, bringing Centre Pompidou’s spirit to new audiences.

The [Public Information Library (Bpi)](https://www.centrepompidou.fr/en/lieu/bpi) moves to the 12th arrondissement of Paris, into the Lumière building, which opens its doors on August 25, 2025, with the same hours and access conditions. As for Centre’s cinema and the Bpi's "Cinémathèque du documentaire" activities, they will be hosted at the mk2 bibliothèque, BNF-François Mitterand entrance, refurbished and renamed [mk2 bibliothèque x Centre Pompidou](https://www.centrepompidou.fr/en/lieu/mk2-bibliotheque-x-centre-pompidou) for the occasion, starting in September 2025. Studio 13/16 will relocate in spring 2026 to a nearby location—the Gaîté Lyrique in the 3rd arrondissement. Only Ircam will remain in its historic location on Place Stravinsky, at the heart of a cultural activation program led by Centre Pompidou, ensuring that the Plateau Beaubourg (Beaubourg neighborhood) continues to be a vibrant cultural hub.

#### On an international scale

Historically known for its generous practice of lending works abroad, Centre Pompidou has, over the past decade, developed an original and ambitious model of international development, extending its reach from Málaga to Shanghai, via Brussels, Seoul and Foz do Iguaçu in Brazil through medium-term collaborations. ## Centre Pompidou Francilien – fabrique de l’art opens in 2027

In spring 2027, a brand-new space dedicated to experiencing art and culture will open its doors in the Île-de-France region. Located in Massy, in Essonne, Centre Pompidou Francilien – fabrique de l’art has been conceived as a hybrid project:

- A professional facility, designed to house the reserves of the Musée National d’Art Moderne and to serve as a hub for research and scientific expertise in the conservation and restoration of artworks;
- A cultural venue, with spaces for exhibitions and mediation, creation and experimentation, conceived as a living extension of the reserves, as close as possible to the making of the Museum and its professions.

Designed by the architectural firm PCA-Stream, this innovative, restrained and resilient building is intended to become a true living space for the residents of the Île-de-France region, just 30 minutes from Paris thanks to the forthcoming Line 18 of the Grand Paris Express. Just as Centre Pompidou in Beaubourg opens onto the city through its Piazza and iconic escalator, Centre Pompidou Francilien engages in dialogue with its immediate environment: nature. Extending towards the Parc de la Blanchette and its lake, its façade features large wooden walkways, a planted stairway, and a panoramic terrace.

# Whistler. Dandy and Disruptor

Meet James McNeill Whistler (1834–1903): painter and printmaker, influencer avant la lettre, aesthete and enfant terrible. _Whistler. Dandy and Disruptor_ is the first retrospective in the Netherlands devoted to this remarkable artist.

[More exhibitions](https://www.vangoghmuseum.nl/en/visit/whats-on/exhibitions)

- Exhibition Whistler. Dandy and Disruptor
- From 16 October 2026
- Until 10 January 2027

[Book tickets](https://tickets.vangoghmuseum.nl/en/whistler/tickets?promo_creative=button&promo_pos=www-vgm&promo_name=tickets&promo_id=www-vgm-tickets-button&_gl=1*2dn9uw*_gcl_au*NzM4NDYwNTExLjE3ODE1MDcwMDI.*_ga*ODA0Nzc1NDE2LjE3NDE5NjEyMzU.*_ga_SB3MZVR8HS*czE3ODM5Mjg4NjEkbzIxNCRnMSR0MTc4Mzk0NDk0MSRqMzEkbDAkaDA.)

[Book tickets](https://tickets.vangoghmuseum.nl/en/whistler/tickets?promo_creative=button&promo_pos=www-vgm&promo_name=tickets&promo_id=www-vgm-tickets-button&_gl=1*2dn9uw*_gcl_au*NzM4NDYwNTExLjE3ODE1MDcwMDI.*_ga*ODA0Nzc1NDE2LjE3NDE5NjEyMzU.*_ga_SB3MZVR8HS*czE3ODM5Mjg4NjEkbzIxNCRnMSR0MTc4Mzk0NDk0MSRqMzEkbDAkaDA.)

James McNeill Whistler is one of the most important artists of the 19th century. With his belief that art – like music – should above all evoke a mood, he helped shape modern art. Alongside his paintings, he is also renowned for his many etchings and drawings, made in cities such as Paris, Amsterdam and Venice. c

Whistler’s rebellious nature and strong convictions regularly set him on a collision course with critics and patrons. With his distinctive and innovative art, he was at times considered too progressive – even by avant-garde artists. Whistler spent months, sometimes even years, working on a single artwork, while the final work appears almost effortless.

At the time, the influential English art historian Roger Fry wrote about Whistler:

> ‘… he seemed to be always inaugurating a revolution, leading intransigent youth against the strongholds of tradition and academic complacence.’

##### Whistler & Van Gogh

Vincent van Gogh admired Whistler and mentioned his etchings in various letters. He counted Whistler among the artists he and his brother Theo had ‘loved in our time’.

Whistler and Van Gogh shared a fascination with Japanese aesthetics and pushed the boundaries of what art could be. Van Gogh referred to the famous portrait of Whistler’s mother in a letter to his sister Willemien, writing:

> ‘There’s a painting that Whistler did of his mother which is like that. But above all in our old Dutch paintings we find it sometimes. When I think of Mother she too appears like that to me.’

##### Audio tour

Would you like to know more about the life and work of James McNeill Whistler? This exhibition is accompanied by a unique audio tour. Find out fascinating stories about the artworks.

You can easily book the audio tour online, together with your entrance ticket.

James Abbott McNeill Whistler, _Arrangement in Grey and Black: Portrait of the Painter's Mother_, 1871, Musée d'Orsay, Paris, Photocredit: © Musée d’Orsay / RMN-Grand Palais / Patrice Schmidt

##### Whistler in five stories

Who was the man behind the art? What made his paintings so innovative? And what did Vincent van Gogh admire about his work? Find out in our exclusive email series. Over five days, you'll receive a fascinating story each day about Whistler, his art and his connection to Van Gogh.

## Discover more

[**Painting Workshops**\\ \\ Join a painting workshop and make your own Nocturne (night landscape).](https://www.vangoghmuseum.nl/en/visit/whats-on/painting-workshops)

[**Guided Tours**\\ \\ During the exhibition tour, a museum guide takes you into Whistler’s world.](https://www.vangoghmuseum.nl/en/visit/whats-on/tours/whistler-tours)

[**Whistler & Music**\\ \\ What music inspired James McNeill Whistler? Discover the link between music and Whistler’s art.](https://www.vangoghmuseum.nl/en/visit/whats-on/exhibitions/whistler/whistler-and-music)

##### Tate Britain

This retrospective was realised in collaboration with Tate Britain in London. The exhibition _[James McNeill Whistler](https://www.tate.org.uk/whats-on/tate-britain/whistler)_, which received widespread critical acclaim, was on display there from 21 May to 27 September 2026.

The Independent: ★★★★★

> ‘Some of the most hauntingly beautiful paintings ever created.’

The Guardian: ★★★★★

> ‘A luscious, seductive blockbuster for the painter who scandalised Britain.’

##### _Whistler. Loving the Netherlands_

The exhibition _[Whistler. Loving the Netherlands](https://www.demesdagcollectie.nl/en/visit/whats-on/exhibition-whistler-loving-the-netherlands)_ runs concurrently at The Mesdag Collection in The Hague, focusing on Whistler’s time in the Netherlands and work he produced during his visits.
